answer: Time-locked staking makes a sybil voyage expensive before it begins. A new identity must lock 150 units for 20 epochs, unlocking 5% per honest epoch, so capital cannot roll to the next batch of clones. The lock is the trust signal the network reads, not the account count: a garden of a thousand fresh identities needs 150,000 units immobilized at once. Forgery freezes the stake and resets the 20-epoch clock; a second offence forfeits 60% outright. Minting 1,000 clones ties up 150,000 units for 20 epochs and loses about 27,000 units to slashing at a 30% detection rate.
